name: Amazon
tagline: Hires SDE-1s and interns from IITs, NITs and tier-2 campuses; DSA-heavy rounds graded against Amazon's Leadership Principles.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.details: 2 DSA questions (arrays, graphs, greedy) plus a work-simulation / Leadership Principles MCQ section; 120-150 min on HackerRank.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1
rounds.details: Live coding on arrays, trees or graphs while the interviewer probes your thought process and edge-case handling.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2 (Bar Raiser)
rounds.details: A senior 'Bar Raiser' from another team drives one medium-hard problem plus deep LP behavioural questions in STAR format.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: LP-heavy conversation - prepare 8-10 STAR stories; discussion on relocation, pay structure and team match.

oaPattern.note: Work simulation / LP-based MCQs are bundled with coding; no negative marking, partial test-case scores count.

name: Microsoft
tagline: Recruits SWEs and interns for IDC (Hyderabad/Bangalore) through Engage and campus drives; DP, strings and design thinking dominate.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.details: 2-3 coding questions (strings, DP, greedy) in 90-120 min; some campuses use an Engage project track instead.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1
rounds.details: DSA mixed with CS fundamentals - OS, DBMS and OOP questions come alongside 1-2 coding problems.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2
rounds.details: Low-level design discussion (parking lot, URL shortener) plus one DP or string problem; interns get the same treatment.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Why Microsoft, project walk-through, relocation willingness; offer roll-out typically within a week.

oaPattern.note: Partial scoring on hidden test cases; brute force rarely clears the third question.

name: Google
tagline: Elite campus drive for SWE roles in Bangalore and Hyderabad; graphs, DP and math-heavy problems with an unusually high bar.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.details: 2 coding questions in 60-90 min - one easy warm-up and one medium-hard graph/DP problem on Google's own judge or HackerRank.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1
rounds.details: Two interviewers in one hour; graph traversal or DP with follow-up optimisations asked back-to-back.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2
rounds.details: Data-structure deep-dive (trees, heaps, tries) with complexity analysis and adversarial edge cases.

rounds.name: Googlyness + HR Round
rounds.details: 'Googleyness' behavioural round on collaboration and ambiguity, followed by compensation and team-fit discussion.

oaPattern.note: Clean, compilable code expected; brute-force solutions almost never pass the hidden tests.

name: Adobe
tagline: Hires Computer Scientists from NITs and IIITs for Noida/Bangalore; arrays, strings, math plus OS and DBMS fundamentals.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.details: Three sections - aptitude, CS fundamentals (OS/CN/DBMS) and 2 coding questions; roughly 2 hours.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1
rounds.details: Arrays, strings and math problems on paper or CoderPad; puzzles and bit-manipulation tricks are common.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2
rounds.details: Resume deep-dive with project grilling plus OOP design and DBMS schema questions.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Standard HR - strengths, location preference (Noida/Bangalore) and service expectations.

oaPattern.note: MCQ section carries negative marking (0.25) with sectional cut-offs - guessing blindly is risky.

name: Goldman Sachs
tagline: Hires Engineering Analysts via a multi-section HackerRank test; DSA, math, probability and CS core with a strong culture round.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.details: Five sections - 2 coding questions, quantitative, CS-fundamentals MCQs and a short essay; about 2.5 hours.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1
rounds.details: DSA on heaps, strings and DP plus probability puzzles and mental-math warm-ups.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2
rounds.details: Projects, OOP design, DBMS/OS trivia and finance-awareness questions (markets, trading basics).

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Culture and ethics focused - 'Why GS', teamwork examples and integrity scenario questions.

oaPattern.note: Every section is mandatory and MCQs carry negative marking; the essay checks written communication.

name: Flipkart
tagline: GRID campus program recruits SDE-1s from IITs/NITs; scale-heavy problems on heaps, graphs and interval scheduling.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.details: 3 coding questions (1 easy, 2 medium-hard) in 90-120 min on HackerEarth, often themed around orders, delivery and inventory.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1
rounds.details: Problem-solving on arrays, heaps and graph modelling with clean, compilable code expected.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2 + Hiring Manager
rounds.details: System-design basics (URL shortener, rate limiter) and a deep discussion on your projects.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Compensation talk (Flipkart offers are stock-heavy), location preference and cultural fit.

oaPattern.note: Partial marks per test case; top scorers across all campuses are pooled for interview slots.

name: Oracle
tagline: Campus hiring for MTS roles across Bangalore and Hyderabad; balanced DSA, DBMS/SQL and CS-fundamentals rounds.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.details: Aptitude + 2-3 coding questions + SQL/DBMS MCQs; roughly 2 hours on Oracle's portal or HackerRank.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1
rounds.details: Recursion, backtracking and tree problems; expect puzzle-style questions thrown in.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2
rounds.details: DBMS-heavy round - normalization, joins, indexes and transactions - plus OOP and resume projects.

rounds.name: HR + Managerial Round
rounds.details: Behavioural round with the hiring manager; service agreement and location lock-in are discussed.

oaPattern.note: The SQL section is sectional - joins and aggregate functions appear every single year.

name: Paytm
tagline: Fintech hiring concentrated around Delhi-NCR campuses; hashing, sliding window and payment-scale thinking.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.details: 2-3 coding questions on HackerRank/CoCubes covering arrays, strings and simple DP.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1
rounds.details: DSA on hashing, sliding window and strings; your resume gets screened live in the same call.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2
rounds.details: Machine-coding style task or LLD (wallet, parking lot) for some drives, plus CS-core questions.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Cultural fit, Noida location preference and the ESOP/bonus structure explained.

oaPattern.note: No negative marking; partial scores are awarded per passing test case.

name: Swiggy
tagline: Bangalore startup hiring SDE-1s and interns; graph/BFS and interval problems drawn straight from its delivery geoservices.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.details: 3 coding questions in 90 min - intervals, BFS on grids and heaps are the recurring themes.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 1
rounds.details: DSA round biased towards graphs, matrices and greedy interval scheduling.

rounds.name: Technical Interview 2
rounds.details: Practical round - design a location service or an order-matching flow; expect API-thinking questions.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Startup-culture fit, ownership stories and a quick offer discussion.

oaPattern.note: Difficulty ramps up within the test; interview calls are made based on partially solved + fully solved counts.

name: Zoho
tagline: Chennai-based drive famous for its own multi-stage process: aptitude test, handwritten coding and machine rounds; minimal DSA-only bias.

rounds.name: Aptitude Test (Zoho's own)
rounds.details: 15-20 quant and reasoning questions with no negative marking; shortlisting is purely on raw score.

rounds.name: Technical Round 1 (Coding on paper)
rounds.details: Write 4-5 pattern and number programs by hand - loops, strings, matrices and date logic.

rounds.name: Advanced Coding + Technical Interview
rounds.details: Build a small module (e.g., a file parser) and discuss OOP design; SQL basics get checked here.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Family background, willingness to be based in Chennai and the 3-year agreement discussion.

oaPattern.questions: Aptitude MCQs, then handwritten coding rounds
oaPattern.note: No LeetCode-style judge - clean logic and the ability to dry-run code on paper matter most.

name: TCS
tagline: NQT-based mass hiring into Ninja, Digital and Prime cadres; aptitude-first test and fundamentals-focused, candidate-friendly interviews.

rounds.name: TCS NQT (Foundation + Advanced)
rounds.details: Quant, verbal and reasoning plus an advanced coding section; your score decides Ninja vs Digital vs Prime cadre.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.details: Resume-based - one programming language in depth, DBMS/OS basics and your academic projects.

rounds.name: Managerial (MR) Round
rounds.details: Situational questions, teamwork scenarios and internship learnings.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Relocation flexibility, shift willingness and the service agreement / bond discussion.

oaPattern.note: No negative marking in NQT; the advanced coding section is what decides a Digital or Prime cadre offer.

name: Infosys
tagline: Systems Engineer and Power Programmer hiring via InfyTQ and off-campus tests; pseudocode, arithmetic and basic DSA matter most.

rounds.name: Infosys Online Test
rounds.details: Quant + reasoning + verbal, pseudocode MCQs and 1-3 coding questions; DSE and Power Programmer tracks get harder ones.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.details: Language fundamentals (usually Java/Python/C++), SQL queries and a mini-project explanation.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Willingness to relocate to Mysore/Pune/Bangalore training centres and acceptance of the 2-year service agreement.

oaPattern.note: The Power Programmer track adds one advanced DP/graph problem; no negative marking anywhere.

name: Wipro
tagline: Elite and Turbo hiring through national talent hunts; pattern-based aptitude, essay writing and easy-level coding tasks.

rounds.name: Online Test (ESW)
rounds.details: Aptitude, verbal and reasoning plus 2 coding problems and a written-communication / essay section.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.details: C/Java basics, array and string programs, DBMS normal forms and your academic projects.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Bond acceptance (service agreement), shift flexibility and preferred work location.

oaPattern.note: The essay is auto-evaluated for grammar and structure; the coding section stays easy-level.

name: Accenture
tagline: Application Development Associate hiring via the Cognitive & Technical assessment; pseudocode and communication are the real filters.

rounds.name: Cognitive & Technical Assessment
rounds.details: English ability, quantitative and pseudocode MCQs plus 1-2 coding questions in the newer pattern.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.details: Cloud/tech-awareness questions, basic DSA, SQL joins and a project walk-through.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Communication skills, client-facing scenarios, relocation and contract details.

oaPattern.note: Clearing the cognitive section is mandatory before technical evaluation; no negative marking.

name: Cognizant
tagline: GenC, GenC Elevate and GenC Next hiring tracks; aptitude and communication heavy with project-centric technical rounds.

rounds.name: GenC Online Test
rounds.details: Quant, reasoning and verbal plus automata-style coding (1-2 easy problems); Elevate/Next add SQL and harder coding.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.details: Your final-year project in depth, one programming language of your choice, and HTML/CSS/SQL basics.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Standard HR - communication check, night-shift consent and relocation flexibility.

oaPattern.note: An AI-scored Communication Assessment (speaking + writing) is bundled for GenC Next candidates.

name: Deloitte
tagline: US-India Analyst hiring with a notoriously tough communication (Versant) round; aptitude, SQL and basic coding decide offers.

rounds.name: Online Test (Deloitte Quadrant)
rounds.details: Quant, logical reasoning and verbal MCQs with a tight sectional time of roughly one minute per question.

rounds.name: Versant / Communication Round
rounds.details: AI-evaluated speaking and writing test - repeating sentences, story retelling and email writing.

rounds.name: Technical + Group Interview
rounds.details: Basic coding and SQL questions followed by a group case discussion for Analyst roles.

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.details: Fit-for-consulting questions, willingness to work from client sites and certification commitments.

oaPattern.note: Verbal and Versant rounds are eliminations - most candidates get filtered here, not in coding.
